audit_findings.title: The perimeter ruling is chronologically impossible
audit_findings.magnitude: NSI purchase price $3,008.1 million; total debt increased $3,047.2 million from FY2025 year-end to June 30, 2026; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE reflects the FY2025 perimeter, while the shares and balance-sheet bridge reflect the post-NSI perimeter; acquired OE, transaction costs and financing must be synchronized.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 1, 2025, the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding equity of Power Rose Acquisition, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Power Rose" and together with its subsidiaries, "DMC Power") for approximately $ 829 million, net of cash acquired, subject to customary purchase price adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated chronology and perimeter error. NSI closed June 9, 2026, not during FY2025. FY2025 instead included Ventev, Nicor and a partial year of DMC Power. Omitting NSI earnings understates value, while omitting its integration and financing burden overstates value. Because the $3.0 billion transaction materially changed the business and financing perimeter, the net direction cannot be established from the current model.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the acquisition ledger through September 5, 2026 and rerun on one coherent basis: either pre-NSI using the December 2025 bridge, or post-NSI using filed pro-forma NSI earnings, amortization, transaction costs, interest and current diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Current acquisition debt interest is missing from the earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: total debt increase $3,047.2 million; filed NSI pro-forma additional interest expense $57.0 million for six months of 2025 and $48.2 million for six months of 2026, annualizing to $114.0 million and $96.4 million, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: An equity-level OE numerator must include interest and financing fees on the same debt and acquisition perimeter represented by the current bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had $2,036.3 million and $1,442.7 million, respectively, of long-term debt outstanding, net of unamortized discount and the unamortized balance of capitalized debt issuance costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated. The $929.9 million FY2025 anchor cannot contain the interest burden from debt issued in June 2026. The filed pro-forma interest adjustments annualize to roughly 10.4%-12.3% of the anchor, before resolving commercial-paper rates and recurring financing-fee amortization, so the omission is reasonably capable of materially overstating equity value.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-close OE using NSI operating results and all associated interest together, including the $900 million term loan, $1.9 billion senior notes, commercial paper and recurring debt-fee amortization; remove the $7.2 million one-time bridge-financing charge unless the model intentionally retains transaction costs.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-funded growth may be credited without its recurring reinvestment cost
audit_findings.magnitude: acquisition spending $958.3 million in 2025 and $1,211.7 million in 2023; base-versus-bear value difference $81.39 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If forecast growth requires recurring acquisitions, the purchase cash needed to obtain that growth is a reinvestment requirement against OE rather than distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Part of the Company’s growth strategy involves acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved forecast dependency, not a demonstrated omission: first-half 2026 organic sales grew 9.2%, but the record does not establish that 6%-8% OE growth can be sustained organically for the forecast period. Materiality is demonstrated by acquisition spending exceeding the $929.9 million anchor in both cited acquisition years and by the $81.39-per-share difference between the zero-growth and 6% scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical OE growth into organic, acquired and divestiture components; then rerun either with an organically supportable growth rate or with a normalized acquisition cash requirement sufficient to produce the assumed growth.

audit_findings.title: The FIFO transition may inflate both the anchor and the ten-year trend
audit_findings.magnitude: FIFO increased 2025 net income by $47.8 million, equal to 5.1% of the $929.9 million anchor, while changing operating cash flow by $0; older-series effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A mixed LIFO/FIFO history can distort trend growth, while an earnings-derived anchor can retain the $47.8 million accounting benefit unless cash working-capital reinvestment offsets it.
audit_findings.evidence: In the second quarter of 2025, the Company elected to change its method of accounting for certain inventory in the U.S. from last in, first out ("LIFO") to first in, first out ("FIFO").
audit_findings.explanation: The $47.8 million accounting effect is demonstrated, but an OE error is not yet demonstrated because filed operating cash flow was unchanged. The record also does not identify the inventory basis used for each year of the ten-year OE series. A possible trend distortion could affect the growth cases, but its magnitude cannot be established without reconstructing the series.
audit_findings.action: Document the source filing, inventory basis and OE formula for every historical year; recast all years consistently and rerun the trend and anchor, explicitly showing whether FIFO's income effect cancels through working capital.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement claims may require cash beyond recorded pension expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $99.5 million pension deficit plus $12.8 million unfunded other benefits equals $112.3 million, or $2.10 per diluted share and 0.71% of $15,810 million base equity value; 2025 contributions exceeded pension cost by $22.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured excess pension funding would reduce OE; alternatively, an unfunded senior claim could be deducted in the equity bridge if not already reflected in forecast expense and cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025 and 2024, we contributed $41.4 million and $1.3 million , respectively, to our qualified foreign and domestic defined benefit pension plans.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE calculation used actual contributions or accounting expense remains unresolved, but the filed balance-sheet exposure is concretely small relative to the valuation. Even deducting the entire $112.3 million deficit reduces base value by only $2.10 per share. The unusually high 2025 contribution also does not establish a recurring requirement: first-half 2026 contributions were only $1.4 million and the filing said anticipated 2026 funding was not significant to liquidity.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE treatment of the $41.4 million 2025 contribution and monitor required contributions; no valuation rerun is necessary unless actuarial evidence establishes recurring excess funding materially above recorded pension cost.

audit_findings.title: A restructuring-related tax benefit may have been capitalized as permanent
audit_findings.magnitude: international-restructuring component unquantified; the entire 2025 Foreign Tax Effect line was an $11.4 million benefit, equal to 1.2% of anchor OE and approximately $3.53 per share if removed proportionally from base operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit raises after-tax anchor OE and is propagated through forecast years and terminal value if the anchor tax rate is left unnormalized.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective tax rate decreased to 20.3% in 2025 compared to 22.1% in 2024, primarily due to a larger income tax benefit in 2025 from international restructurings as compared to the prior year, as well as the income tax costs from the sale of our residential lighting business in the first quarter of 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that international restructuring contributed to the lower 2025 tax rate, but it does not isolate the restructuring amount within the $11.4 million Foreign Tax Effect line. Even treating that entire line as nonrecurring would reduce the base value by only about $3.53 per share, approximately 1.2%, which is not enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-footnote or workpaper breakdown of the international-restructuring benefit and normalize the anchor cash tax rate; rerun only if the isolated recurring-rate adjustment materially exceeds the filed $11.4 million Foreign Tax Effect line.
